title: Memory minimum for the four-round Even--Mansour tradeoff curve
summary: Determine the least memory that can retain the source four-round two-key Even--Mansour attack curve, including the highlighted low-memory EC9 regime.

formal_statement.body: Let $N=2^n$ and consider the non-weak four-round two-key iterated Even--Mansour schedule classes analyzed by the source in the known-plaintext model. Determine the minimum asymptotic memory $M(D)$ for a key-recovery attack that retains total time $T=N^2/D$ (up to the source's ignored polynomial factors) for each admissible data size $D\le N$. In particular, for EC9 with round-key sequence $[K_0,K_1,K_0,K_0,K_1]$ and $N^{1/2}<D\le N$, decide whether an attack with $M<N$ and $T=N^2/D$ exists, or prove a matching lower bound on $M$.

scope.domain: Known-plaintext key-recovery attacks on source-defined four-round two-key iterated Even--Mansour schedule classes
assumptions: The public round permutations, key schedules and non-weak schedule classes are those defined by the source
Only known plaintext--ciphertext pairs are available
Preprocessing and online work count toward total time
Multiplicative polynomial factors in n are ignored as in the source
The EC9 instance uses round-key sequence [K0,K1,K0,K0,K1]
scope.unresolved_remainder: The complete minimum-memory function for the source schedule classes remains unknown. The explicitly emphasized remainder is EC9 with N^(1/2)<D<=N: whether M<N is possible at unchanged T=N^2/D, or whether a matching lower bound rules it out.

provenance.note: The first archived ePrint version received 2013-10-24 contains the EC9 memory question and the corresponding general memory-minimization direction.
